items.h: Listed as questionable, won't start
items.s: Watson (concussion) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Saints, but Shedeur Sanders will start even if Watson is active Kelsey Russo of the Browns' official site reports. Per Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com, coach Todd Monken said Friday that he hasn't decided if Watson will be the team's Week 9 backup, as the QB -- who is in the NFL's concussion protocol -- has yet to be cleared. In any case, if Watson is active come Sunday, he'll merely be the backup. He was a limited practice participant Friday, after missing the previous two days.

items.h: Deshaun Watson (concussion) listed questionable Sunday
items.s: Deshaun Watson is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Saints. Watson returned to practice on Friday. He will have till Saturday to clear concussion protocol.

items.h: Deshaun Watson (concussion) practicing Friday
items.s: Deshaun Watson (concussion) is practicing for the Cleveland Browns Friday according to Scott Petrak. Watson remains in the league's concussion protocols, leaving the quarterback's game status in question. Shedeur Sanders would be in line to start behind center against the Saints for head coach Todd Monken if Watson remains sidelined Sunday.

items.h: Returns to practice field Friday
items.s: Watson (concussion) was present for practice Friday, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports. Ian Rapoport of NFL Network previously suggested that Watson "is unlikely to start" Sunday's game against the Saints, but either way, the QB's return to the field, in any capacity, is a positive step toward him advancing through the NFL's concussion protocol. Friday's final injury report will add further clarity to Watson's Week 9 status, but if he isn't cleared to play this weekend, Shedeur Sanders would be in line to start in his place.

items.h: Fantasy buzz: Jags score 30 but fizzle in fantasy; Wentz to start for Vikings
items.s: The Jaguars were solidly in control Thursday night, but that did not translate to big fantasy performances.

items.h: Unlikely to start Sunday
items.s: Watson (concussion) "is unlikely to start" Sunday's game against the Saints, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports. Watson has not practiced since being placed in the NFL's concussion protocol Tuesday, and it appears he will not be cleared to suit up for Week 9. The Browns will provide an official update on Watson's status later Friday, and if he is unable to go, Shedeur Sanders would presumably get the start in his place.

items.h: Deshaun Watson Questionable to Play on Sunday
items.s: Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson (concussion) is being listed as questionable to play on Sunday in Week 9 against the New Orleans Saints, according to Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN. Watson entered the NFL's concussion protocol earlier this week and missed practice on Wednesday and Thursday, although he returned to the field for Friday's session. Although the veteran signal-caller has not been technically ruled out this weekend, he will not start, as head coach Todd Monken announced that Shedeur Sanders will make the start under center with Watson still in the concussion protocol. If Watson is cleared by Sunday, he will be in a backup role in the Big Easy. Fantasy managers who have been…

items.h: Deshaun Watson Returns to Practice on Friday
items.s: Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson (concussion) returned to practice on Friday as he makes his way through the league's concussion protocol, according to ESPN's Daniel Oyefusi. It is good progress for Watson, but it may be a little too late this week, as it was reported earlier on Friday that he is not expected to be cleared to play in the Week 9 contest on Sunday on the road against the New Orleans Saints. We should have more clarity on Watson's status when the Browns release their official injury report on Friday, but as of now, fantasy managers who have been using him in two-QB leagues should not be planning on having Watson available this weekend. If he is officially ruled…

items.h: Deshaun Watson Not Expected to Play Sunday
items.s: Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson (concussion) is not expected to play in Week 9 against the New Orleans Saints. After finishing the Week 8 game, Watson was placed in concussion protocol on Wednesday and has not practiced this week. With Watson not expected to suit up against the Saints, second-year quarterback Shedeur Sanders is slated to start. In seven career starts, Sanders has completed 116 of 196 passes for 1,353 yards, seven touchdowns, and nine interceptions, along with 20 carries for 170 yards and a touchdown. While this slightly affects the Browns' top playmakers, including KC Concepcion, Denzel Boston, and Harold Fannin Jr., who didn't practice on Thursday, Sanders…

items.h: Deshaun Watson (concussion) not practicing Thursday
items.s: Deshaun Watson remained absent from practice on Thursday. Watson remains in concussion protocol. He is continuing to trend in the wrong direction for Sunday's game against the Saints.

items.h: Fantasy buzz: Vikings to start Wentz, but fantasy managers probably shouldn't
items.s: With the Vikings turning to Carson Wentz on Monday, how does that change the outlook for the team's WRs?

items.h: Missing another practice
items.s: Watson (concussion) remained sidelined from practice Thursday, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports. With Watson, who is in the NFL's concussion protocol, in line to log back-to-back DNPs, the QB's status for Sunday's game against the Saints remains cloudy. In the event that Watson doesn't gain clearance to play this weekend, Shedeur Sanders will draw the start in his place.

items.h: Deshaun Watson Sidelined From Practice on Thursday
items.s: Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson (concussion) is still not practicing on Thursday after reporting delayed concussion symptoms following a Week 8 loss to the Steelers and landing in the NFL's concussion protocol. Watson has been the fantasy QB17 through eight weeks, but if he is unable to play in a Week 9 matchup with the Saints, Cleveland will turn to second-year quarterback Shedeur Sanders. Sanders threw for less than 200 yards per game across his seven starts in 2025, while averaging a single touchdown per start. He did, however, form an obvious connection with tight end Harold Fannin Jr., while his propensity for throwing underneath could also help provide a usable fantasy…

items.h: Fantasy buzz: Wilson in protocol, Tuten GTD for TNF, four teams make QB changes
items.s: Two sure fantasy starters are unsure to play this week, while QB news was plentiful.

items.h: Deshaun Watson (concussion) officially doesn't practice Wednesday
items.s: Deshaun Watson (concussion) officially did not practice for the Browns on Wednesday. Watson was placed in the NFL's concussion protocol on Wednesday, so it's not at all surprising that he was a non-participant at practice. It looks all but guaranteed that he will be sidelined this week, which will leave Shedeur Sanders as the starting quarterback for the Browns in his absence. That would be a somewhat lateral move for Cleveland's fantasy-relevant pass catchers.

items.h: Unable to practice Wednesday
items.s: The Browns listed Watson (concussion) as a non-participant in Wednesday's practice. Early in this past Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers, Watson exited the game to get checked for a concussion following a helmet-to-helmet hit, but he was cleared to re-enter the contest after missing just four offensive snaps. However, after he had some late-surfacing symptoms, Watson entered concussion protocol Tuesday and was a spectator for the Browns' first Week 9 session. According to Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com, Watson "felt a lot better" Wednesday and was involved in meetings, but Shedeur Sanders took all the reps with the first-team offense. Sanders appears to be trending toward starting Sunday…

items.h: Fantasy buzz: Watson, Wilson enter concussion protocol ahead of Week 9
items.s: How do the potential absences of Deshaun Watson and Garrett Wilson impact the players around them?

items.h: May not clear concussion protocol in time
items.s: Mary Kay Cabot of the Cleveland Plain Dealer suggests that Watson may have difficulty clearing the NFL's concussion protocol ahead of Sunday's game against the Saints. In the wake of Wednesday's news that Watson is in the protocol, the Browns' Week 9 QB situation will be worth monitoring closely as Sunday's 1:00 pm ET kickoff approaches. Key context on that front will arrive via the team's upcoming practice report, but if Watson is unable to gain clearance to play this weekend, Shedeur Sanders would be in line to get his first regular-season start.

items.h: Trending toward sitting out Week 9
items.s: Watson is expected to face an uphill battle to clear concussion protocol prior to Sunday's game against the Saints, leaving Shedeur Sanders as the Browns' likely Week 9 starting quarterback, Mary Kay Cabot of the Cleveland Plain Dealer reports. After reporting concussion symptoms Tuesday following Sunday's loss to the Steelers, Watson entered the protocol and isn't expected to practice Wednesday. Sanders will take all of the first-team reps Wednesday, and unless Watson can pass through the protocol quickly, the Browns will prepare for the second-year signal-caller to direct the offense in Week 9.

items.h: Deshaun Watson in the concussion protocol
items.s: Deshaun Watson has been placed in the concussion protocol. Watson took a big hit early in Sunday's loss to the Steelers, but he returned to the game just a few plays later after being cleared by medical. The Cleveland QB experienced some lingering symptoms earlier this week, however, leading the team to place him in the protocol. Watson does reportedly have at least a chance of returning for Sunday's game in New Orleans, but time will ultimately tell. Sheduer Sanders would take over at QB if Watson cannot go.

items.h: Placed in concussion protocol
items.s: The Browns announced Wednesday that Watson has been placed in concussion protocol. Watson took a helmet-to-helmet hit in the first quarter of Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers, and after being examined by an independent consultant he was cleared to return to the game. Though subsequent tests after the game and Monday morning showed no symptoms of a concussion, Watson informed the Browns on Tuesday morning that he was experiencing symptoms and was "immediately placed in the concussion protocol," per the team. Watson will need to clear the five-step protocol in order to play in Cleveland's Week 9 matchup with New Orleans, but if he's unable to go, Shedeur Sanders would be in line to start…

items.h: Deshaun Watson not practicing Wednesday, remains optimistic for Sunday
items.s: Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson (concussion) is not expected to practice on Wednesday after entering the NFL's concussion protocol this week, according to Scott Petrak of The Elyria Chronicle-Telegram. However, head coach Todd Monken is not ruling Watson out, and he is optimistic that he will play on Sunday on the road against the New Orleans Saints, who are coming off their bye. Fantasy managers who have been using the 31-year-old veteran in two-QB superflex leagues should be formulating a backup plan for this week. If Watson cannot get cleared from the protocol by the start of the weekend, second-year signal-caller Shedeur Sanders would be in line for his first start of the…

items.h: Deshaun Watson Placed in Concussion Protocol Wednesday
items.s: Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson (concussion) was placed in concussion protocol on Wednesday, according to Mary Kay Cabot. Watson left Week 8's game against the Pittsburgh Steelers early after hitting his head on the turf in the first quarter. Second-year quarterback Shedeur Sanders replaced him for a drive, but Watson returned and finished the game. With Watson in the protocol, it's unclear whether he will be able to suit up for Week 9's contest against the New Orleans Saints, which would put Sanders in line to start. In seven career starts, Sanders has completed 116 of 196 passes for 1,353 yards, seven touchdowns, and nine interceptions, while adding 153 yards and a touchdown…

items.h: Deshaun Watson Not a Trustworthy Streamer in Single-QB Leagues
items.s: Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson has had an encouraging start to the 2026 season compared to the rest of his tenure in Cleveland, coming in at QB20 (minimum three games played) with 15.6 fantasy points per game so far. This puts him firmly in the conversation as a starter in two QB leagues. He passed for seven touchdowns in the first five weeks, but has since slowed down, scoring only one touchdown in the last three, and it was rushing. In Weeks 7 and 8, Watson passed for 308 and 324 yards, respectively, but the passing touchdowns did not come. The Browns' Week 9 opponent, the New Orleans Saints, allow the ninth-most passing yards per game (249.7 yards) and have given up 11…

items.h: Deshaun Watson throws for 324 yards Sunday
items.s: Deshaun Watson completed 27-of-39 passes for 324 yards in the Browns 27-6 loss against the Steelers. Watson did not throw a touchdown or interception, but he did lose a fumble. He was also sacked eight times. Watson will be a QB2 play next week against the Saints.

items.h: Over 300 passing yards in loss
items.s: Watson completed 27 of 39 passes for 324 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions while rushing three times for two yards in the Browns' 27-6 loss to the Steelers on Sunday. He also lost a fumble. Watson couldn't lead the Browns to a single touchdown, but he exceeded 300 passing yards for the second straight game since Cleveland was forced into a pass-centric approach. Watson displayed the most chemistry with Harold Fannin (10-154-0 on 12 targets), and he recorded completions to seven different targets overall. Watson also lost the handle on a combined sack by Patrick Queen and Cameron Heyward in the first quarter, which led to a Steelers touchdown. Watson will look to rebound in a…

items.h: Back in Sunday's game
items.s: Watson (undisclosed) returned to Sunday's game in Pittsburgh, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports. Watson endured a big hit on the Browns' first offensive possession and was required to visit the medical tent for what likely was to check on a possible concussion. He's since been cleared to return to action.

items.h: Visits sideline tent in Week 8
items.s: Watson went to the sideline tent in the first quarter of Sunday's game at Pittsburgh, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports. Watson took a big hit on the Browns' first offensive possession, and it appears he may be undergoing a check for a possible concussion. Shedeur Sanders will take over for Watson for as long as the latter is sidelined.

items.h: Deshaun Watson Returns to Game vs. Steelers
items.s: Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson (head) returned to the game against the Pittsburgh Steelers after briefly exiting in the first quarter for a concussion check, according to Kelsey Russo, an associate editor and staff writer for the Browns. Shedeur Sanders replaced Watson while he was out. On the first drive following Watson's return, he was strip-sacked by Pittsburgh linebacker Patrick Queen, and the ball was recovered by Pittsburgh defensive lineman Keeanu Benton, which eventually led to a touchdown for the Steelers.

items.h: Deshaun Watson Headed to Medical Tent for Concussion Check
items.s: Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson (head) is heading to the medical tent after a roughing-the-passer call on Pittsburgh Steelers safety Jaquan Brisker in Week 8, according to The Athletic's Mike DeFabo. Scott Petrak of The Chronicle-Telegram and Medina Gazette adds that the referees sent Watson to the sideline for concussion evaluation. Shedeur Sanders is now in at quarterback for the Browns. Watson's status will need to be monitored moving forward.

items.h: Deshaun Watson Not Looking Like Front-Line Starting QB
items.s: Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson looks to be on the low end of starting quarterbacks for fantasy in his Week 8 matchup at the Pittsburgh Steelers. Watson has led the Browns to 5-2 overall record but his fantasy numbers leave something to be desired this season. Watson was 25-of-36 passing in Week 7's win over the Titans with 308 passing yards and an interception without a touchdown. He did rush three times for 19 yards and a rushing touchdown. Although he didn't find the end zone passing the ball, it was one of Watson's better games through the air. He will likely find things tougher this week against the Steelers' defense, which ranks 11th against the pass allowing 212.7…

items.h: Deshaun Watson's 308 Yards Don't Fix the Touchdown Drought
items.s: Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson threw for 308 yards in Sunday's 27-24 victory over the Tennessee Titans, topping 300 yards for the first time since joining the team, yet he failed to throw a touchdown for the second consecutive game. He completed 25 of 36 passes with one interception and added 19 rushing yards on three carries, including a nine-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter. Over his past three starts, the veteran has thrown just one touchdown pass, which puts his season total at seven through seven games. The legs keep rescuing him, with 215 rushing yards on 48 attempts ranking third among NFL quarterbacks. Week 8 brings a rematch with the Pittsburgh Steelers, against…

items.h: Deshaun Watson throws for 308 yards in Week 7 win
items.s: Deshaun Watson completed 25 of his 36 passes for 308 yards and one interception while adding three rushes for 19 yards and a touchdown in a 27-24 win over the Titans in Week 7. Watson did not throw any touchdowns but he contributed on a nine-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter. The veteran QB only has two touchdown passes over his last four games but he did just enough to get the Browns the win in Week 7, completing a key 36-yard pass to Harold Fannin Jr. late in the fourth quarter to set the Browns up for the game-winning field goal. Watson will be a low-end QB2 in Week 8 vs. the Steelers.

items.h: Engineers another comeback win
items.s: Watson completed 25 of 36 passes for 308 yards with an interception in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Titans. He added 19 yards and a touchdown on three carries. While he didn't throw a TD pass for a second straight game, Watson produced a season high in passing yards and scored his first rushing TD since Week 2 of the 2024 season on a nine-yard scamper in the fourth quarter. Watson also led his fifth game-winning, fourth-quarter drive of the year, completing another comeback after the Browns fell behind 14-0 early. The veteran QB will take a 7:3 TD:INT through seven games into a Week 8 meeting with the Steelers.

items.h: Deshaun Watson Worth A Look In Week 7
items.s: Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson is a decent starting option in Week 7's game against the Tennessee Titans. Watson was 16-for-26 passing for 164 yards and no touchdowns and no interceptions in last week's 13-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens. This week he gets a little bit better of a matchup against the Titans, even if it is on the road. The Titans rank in the middle of the pack at 16th in the NFL in pass defense, allowing 220.5 passing yards per game with six passing touchdowns allowed. Watson has 1,174 passing yards this season with seven passing touchdowns compared to just two interceptions. The veteran quarterback needs to show more touchdown ability to be considered a safe…

items.h: Deshaun Watson a Viable QB Streamer to Target on Waivers
items.s: Across six games in 2026, Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson has completed 63.8% of his pass attempts for 1,174 yards, seven touchdowns, and two interceptions. The 31-year-old has also added some fantasy value with his legs, rushing for 196 yards on 45 attempts. After a relatively hot start to the year, Watson's production has slowed down of late. Over the last two weeks, totaled just 319 passing yards and one touchdown while leading the Cleveland offense to just 25 total points. However, the Browns have a significantly easier matchup coming up in Week 7 against the Tennessee Titans. Through six weeks, Tennessee ranks in the bottom 10 in the NFL in yards per pass attempt allowed…

items.h: Compiles 193 scrimmage yards in win
items.s: Watson completed 16 of 26 passes for 164 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions and added eight carries for 29 yards in the Browns' 13-10 win over the Ravens on Sunday. As Watson's numbers suggest, he didn't do anything of particular note as either a passer or runner, but the veteran signal-caller did avoid turnovers despite taking five sacks. That alone helped keep Cleveland in a game in which the Browns faced a 10-0 halftime deficit, and he was then able to lead fourth-quarter touchdown and field-goal drives that completed the comeback. Watson has surprisingly helped the Browns to a 4-2 record, and he's provided a solid 7:2 TD:INT and 196 rushing yards along the way. He'll look to…

items.h: Deshaun Watson quiet in Week 6 win
items.s: Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson completed 16 of his 26 passes for 164 scoreless yards in a 13-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens in Week 6. He added eight carries and 29 yards on the ground. Watson has led the Browns to an AFC North-leading 4-2 start, including a 3-0 record at home. Week 6 was his first without a touchdown and his third game in the last four weeks with fewer than 175 passing yards. The Browns' offense has not been high-octane, and Watson has provided the fantasy output of a QB2.

items.h: Deshaun Watson A Mid-Tier Starting QB For Week 6
items.s: Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson returns home for a Week 6 matchup with the Baltimore Ravens after losing a road contest to the New York Jets last week. Watson was inaccurate overall against the Jets in Week 5, completing 15-of-33 passes for 155 yards and a touchdown pass to wide receiver Denzel Boston. Watson will look to build on and improve his performance from last week back at home against the Ravens. The Ravens' pass defense ranks 18th in the NFL with 223.6 passing yards allowed per game and has allowed just five passing touchdowns this season. Watson has struggled to put up QB1 numbers this season and has a completion rate of 64.2 percent this year with 1,010 passing…

items.h: Deshaun Watson Continues to Produce as a Viable Streaming Option
items.s: Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson has cooled down since the first three weeks of the season, but he still remains in the streaming conversation for fantasy football. Watson has thrown for at least one touchdown pass in every game this season, but he also has three turnovers over the last two weeks. Similarly, although he has been running the ball incredibly well, he has also found himself under extreme pressure; he took a whopping eight sacks in Week 5. It seems like for every positive factor surrounding Watson, there's also something negative to consider. That's why he remains a fringe streamer going forward. He doesn't need to be rostered in every league, but managers looking…

items.h: Inaccurate in Week 5 loss
items.s: Watson completed 15 of 33 passes for 155 yards and a touchdown while rushing six times for 40 yards in Sunday's 17-12 loss to the Jets. He also lost a fumble. Watson orchestrated a go-ahead touchdown drive in the fourth quarter for the fourth consecutive game, giving the Browns a 12-10 lead with a 29-yard touchdown pass to Denzel Boston with 6:15 remaining. Cleveland's defense held up to win the previous three games, but that streak was snapped here, as the Jets scored a go-ahead touchdown with 3:01 remaining while the Browns failed to score on their final three drives, the last of which ended with a Watson fumble on fourth down. Watson and the Browns will take a 3-2 record into a key Week…

items.h: Watson completed 24 of 33 passes for 268 yards with one touchdown and one interception while rushing seven times for 22 yards in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Steelers on Thursday. He also committed two fumbles,…
items.s: Watson's rather unlikely comeback season continued in the primetime spotlight Thursday against a division rival, with the embattled veteran ultimately besting future Hall of Famer Aaron Rodgers. Watson's late third-quarter fumble on a sack by T.J. Watt didn't result in any Steelers points, but his interception on Cleveland's ensuing possession on a deep pass intended for Denzel Boston did lead to Pittsburgh's penultimate touchdown of the night. Watson was otherwise impressive, recording his highest passing yardage total since Week 3 of the 2023 season. Watson connected with seven different…

items.h: Watson completed 16 of 30 passes for 144 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions while rushing 11 times for 45 yards in the Browns' 21-18 win over the Panthers on Sunday. He also threw a two-point conversion pass.
items.s: While Watson was anything but efficient through the air for the majority of the afternoon, the veteran signal-caller avoided turnovers and fired a pair of key touchdown passes to Harold Fannin, including a game-winning scoring toss with 1:48 remaining on which Watson scrambled to buy himself time before releasing the ball on the run. Watson's mobility played a key part throughout earlier portions of the game, as he was second on Cleveland in rushing yards with his highest total since Week 9 of the 2020 season while he was still with the Texans (he'd also rushed for 45 yards in Week 1 of the…

items.h: Watson completed 24 of 30 passes for 238 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions while adding seven rushes for 22 yards in the Browns' 23-19 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
items.s: The proverbial vultures seemed to be surrounding Watson already after an ugly Week 1 loss to the Jaguars, but the oft-maligned veteran signal-caller preserved his starting job for the moment with Sunday's weather-delayed upset victory. Watson ran the Browns offense with a steady hand throughout the afternoon, avoiding turnovers while navigating a pair of sacks and connecting with Denzel Boston (55 yards) and Blake Whiteheart (17 yards) for his pair of touchdown passes. Watson has completed a stellar 76.9 percent of his passes and posted a 3:1 TD:INT through two games, and he'll next take on…

items.h: Head coach Todd Monken said Monday that he anticipates sticking with Watson as the Browns' starting quarterback for Week 2 against the Buccaneers, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports.
items.s: Watson will retain the starting job, despite a poor showing Sunday in the Browns' 34-10 season-opening loss to the Jaguars. While making his first regular-season appearance since Oct. 20, 2024, Watson completed 16 of 22 pass attempts for 205 yards, one touchdown and one interception while rushing six times for 38 yards. Upon reviewing film of the game, Monken said he saw enough positives from Watson to stick with him as the team's starter, though the 31-year-old quarterback likely won't have much job security.
